profile_text.body:
Cerence Inc. is a public company headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts, and trades under the ticker CRNC. Its site describes it as delivering conversational and agentic AI-powered user experiences for automotive and beyond, with tailor-made AI solutions that integrate with vehicle makers' systems while preserving their brand identity. The company says it is moving to advance generative AI and large language model-powered innovation that it believes will be central to the automotive and transportation user experience.

Its AI work centers on CaLLM, described as an advanced family of language models that brings conversational AI to the automotive world, and on Cerence Emergency Vehicle Detection (EVD). The company says EVD is already deployed in production vehicles and can detect and localize more than 1,500 emergency sirens across nearly 50 countries, identifying approaching emergency vehicles from more than 300 meters away with interior microphones and beyond 800 meters when paired with exterior microphones. Cerence also describes dynamic speech enhancement for multi-seat in-car environments, allowing passengers in different zones to make requests at once. In its third quarter results, the company reported revenue up 12% YoY, connected services revenue up 20% YoY, and operating cash flow of $20M supporting its first-ever share repurchase program. Site material also includes a joint piece with Microsoft on Zero Trust and layered AI security for in-car assistants, credited to Kaivan Karimi, Business Development Senior Director at Cerence AI, and Frank Kaleck, Director Industry Advisory Automotive at Microsoft, and a demo presented by Timo Matheja and Stefan Hamerich.

The company's litigation exposure is recorded in Massachusetts, with a count of 97. No product entries, lawsuits, or MCP servers are listed for it.
